claims.text: Recurrent VVC (three or more episodes in a year):
claims.quote: Recurrent VVC (three or more episodes of symptomatic VVC in <1 year)

claims.text: 7–14 days of topical azole, or fluconazole 100, 150 or 200 mg PO every 3rd day for 3 doses;
claims.quote: a longer duration of initial therapy (e.g., 7–14 days of topical therapy or a 100-mg, 150-mg, or 200-mg oral dose of fluconazole every third day for a total of 3 doses [days 1, 4, and 7]) is recommended

claims.text: then fluconazole weekly for 6 mo as maintenance
claims.quote: Oral fluconazole (i.e., a 100-mg, 150-mg, or 200-mg dose) weekly for 6 months is the indicated maintenance regimen.

claims.text: Severe VVC: 7–14 days of topical azole, or fluconazole 150 mg in two sequential oral doses (second dose 72 h after the first)
claims.quote: Either 7–14 days of topical azole or 150 mg of fluconazole in two sequential oral doses (second dose 72 hours after initial dose) is recommended.

claims.text: Compromised host (eg, poorly controlled DM, HIV, corticosteroids): more prolonged (7–14 days) conventional treatment
claims.quote: Women with underlying immunodeficiency, those with poorly controlled diabetes or other immunocompromising conditions (e.g., HIV), and those receiving immunosuppression therapy (e.g., corticosteroid treatment) might not respond as well to short-term therapies. Efforts to correct modifiable conditions should be made, and more prolonged (i.e., 7–14 days) conventional treatment is necessary.

claims.text: Pregnancy: topical azoles for 7 days only;
claims.quote: Only topical azole therapies, applied for 7 days, are recommended for use among pregnant women.

claims.text: don't use oral fluconazole (possible association with spontaneous abortion and congenital anomalies)
claims.quote: Epidemiologic studies indicate a single 150-mg dose of fluconazole might be associated with spontaneous abortion (1150) and congenital anomalies; therefore, it should not be used (1151).

claims.text: Oral azoles can cause nausea, abdominal pain and headache and have clinically important drug interactions;
claims.quote: Oral azoles occasionally cause nausea, abdominal pain, and headache. Therapy with the oral azoles has rarely been associated with abnormal elevations of liver enzymes. Clinically important interactions can occur when oral azoles are administered with other drugs (1141).
claims.locator: Drug Allergy, Intolerance, and Adverse Reactions

claims.text: topical azoles can cause local burning or irritation
claims.quote: Topical agents usually cause no systemic side effects, although local burning or irritation might occur.
